exact_statement: For every Boolean sign on a finite uniform cube, with natural logarithms, K=(H_nat-p_empty ln(1/p_empty))/2=integral J, every physical block B obeys 2[K(f)-E_y K(f_y)]=M_B^++C_B^++ell_B. q_T=sum_{U subset B}p_{U union T}=E_y p_y(T), M_T=sum_U p_{U union T}ln(q_T/p_{U union T}), C_T=E_y p_y(T)ln(p_y(T)/q_T), plus omits T=empty, and ell_B=sum_{nonempty U subset B}p_U ln(1/p_U); all terms nonnegative. This identity telescopes for every finite adaptive block-query tree with terminal K retained. ONLY for singleton-query trees, the cumulative paid channel-plus-level charge is <=beta[I(root)-E I(leaf)], beta=2+2/e^2, because C_i^+<=2(Inf_i-p_{i}) and |hat f({i})|<=Inf_i. No such price is asserted for arbitrary block-query trees. Also 0<=B_nat-R_nat<=(1+2/e)I; R_nat=sum_i M_i^+, B_nat=sum_i H_nat(S_i|S_without_i). For F_m=y product_j g(x^(j)) on disjoint copies, R_nat(F_m)=m B_nat(g), I(F_m)=m I(g)+1. Hence the optimal universal constants for R_nat/I and B_nat/I coincide. A universal R_nat<=A I implies FEI bits constant (A+2)/ln2 via C018; A remains unproved.

exact_statement: For every finite Boolean seed f, every m,k>=1 and ell>=2 on disjoint uniform blocks, let h=chi_Z product_b f_b, J=mI(f)+ell, F=1+A_k(h-1), q=2^-k, d=(1-q)^2+q^2. For each relevant coordinate use mu_i(T)=p_(T+i)/Inf_i and r_i(T)=p_T+p_(T+i); both normalize to one. Let M=sum_i Inf_i[log2(1/Inf_i)-D(mu_i||r_i)] and D_f be the KL divergence of the normalized joint derivative/reference laws, with I(f)D_f=0 for constants. Original core-coordinate divergences obey D_i(F)=D_i(h)+k, D_i(h)=D_i(f) on seed blocks and D_i(h)=0 on parity bits. Every control divergence is D_c=(1-q)(k-1)+q log2(q/d). Consequently I(F)=q(J+k), I(F)D_F=q[mI(f)D_f+kJ+kD_c], M(F)=qmM(f)+k[q(1-q)+q^2 log2(d/q^2)], and M_ge2(F)=qmM(f)+kq(1-kq). For every fixed ell>=2 and finite nonnegative s(N)=o(N), the supremum of M_geell/I over 0<I<=2^-s(N) equals the unrestricted supremum K_M in the extended reals. No finiteness of K_M, universal refund payment or full FEI conclusion is asserted.
